newsitem.title: south africa: Mobutu envoy meets Mandela in Zaire peace move.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu envoy meets Mandela in Zaire peace move.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela on Thursday met a special envoy of Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko to accelerate moves to peace talks for Zaire.
Mandela and Ngbanda Nzambo Ko Ayumba, Mobutu's nephew, both said afterwards talks were continuing, but that utmost confidentiality was needed to ensure their success.
"All I want to say is that there is progress, which is very encouraging," said Mandela, who on Wednesday also met Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila.

Ngabanda said Mobutu was committed to a negotiated solution to the conflict, which began last October when Kabila's rebels took up arms, but declined to say if Mobutu would drop his refusal to talk directly with the rebels.
"President Mobutu himself is committed to finding a peaceful solution to save the lives of innocent people," Ngbanda said.
Mandela's spokesman Parks Mankahlana said earlier Mandela had wanted to meet Ngabanda "to say encouraging words to both sides".
"He is not going to enter negotiations of any sort," Mankahlana added.
Kabila said on Wednesday after meeting Mandela that he hoped direct peace talks could start soon with the Mobutu government.
South Africa, with the help of the United Nations, the United States and fellow African countries, is trying to broker direct peace talks between the two sides.
On Wednesday, African leaders agreed to hold an urgent summit on the crisis on March 18, at a location to be decided.
Kabila's rebel force, many of them Zairean Tutsis whose ethnic kin control neighbouring Rwanda and Burundi, took up arms last October and have overrun eastern Zaire's borderlands.
The conflict escalated this month with the bombing of rebel-held towns and has sent tens of thousands of refugees fleeing, threatening to destabilise Zaire and its neighbours.
